analysis.title: GS US TMT: ... 10 things … 11 Oct 2026
key_insights: NDX is up four weeks in a row and six of the last seven, near all-time highs with VIX in the 14s. Under the surface, software outperformed semis by about 800 bps last week.

Investors expect steady earnings beats across semis and the Mag 7, but are less sure that translates into near-term alpha. Open questions include momentum in the Personal Agent theme. The bull case that compute demand outstrips compute supply still supports confidence in 2027+ capex.
Sentiment is weak. The UoM Consumer Sentiment Index is back at 20+ year lows, and GIR's sentiment indicator shows light equity investor positioning.
Top client inbounds last week: breakouts in AMZN and MSFT, why Analog Semis are heavy, what it takes for Memory to recover, bogeys into TSM, and what is driving Security names (CRWD, PANW) higher.
Non-52-week-high names drawing more questions: ZS, SPOT, RBLX, SE, SPHR, NOW, STX, WDC, AVGO, SPCX, LYV.

Overbought on 14-day RSI: SNPS, P, NTAP, NTNX, HPE, FFIV, OKTA, PLTR, DT, GTLB, DDOG, PD, NTSK, ZS, FTNT, VIA. Oversold on 14-day RSI: INDI, CRUS, SHAZ, ALKT, VRRM, FICO, OPEN, CMCSA, CHTR, VZ, T, SPHR, VSNT.

TSM reports Thursday 10/15 pre-market after its biggest 4-day pullback since late July (down about 7% Tuesday to Friday). Investor focus: 2027+ capex, gross margin outlook, updated supply/demand and revenue visibility around GenAI (XPUs, CPUs, networking), and non-AI commentary on phones, autos and PCs.
GIR models TSM capex at $85bn in 2027E and $98bn in 2028E. It models relatively stable gross margins q/q in 2H versus 2Q, and raises out-year gross margins on milder dilution from the N2 ramp.

Cyclical angst: the GS CYCS v DEFS pair had its worst week since mid-August and the R2K closed lower for a fifth straight week. Cyclical tech and semis are seeing heavier price action, with Analog Semis underperforming their usual relationship with ISM data. The desk frames it as either an opportunity or a warning.

Dell takeaways from GIR's visit (CFO, IR, ISG): management pushed back on AI infrastructure commoditization, supply is the main constraint on AI infrastructure growth, memory is expected to stay constrained into next year, storage and operating leverage drive future margin expansion, and enterprise AI adoption is in the very early innings. Dell FY27 revenue revisions are up nearly 100% over about a year.

Inference economy names (SNOW, CRWD, PANW, NET, PLTR) are at or near all-time highs even as semis stumbled in the second half of last week. Investors see their outlook as tied to AI deployment rather than capex. Clients are asking two-way questions about whether earnings growth will justify the multiples, especially ahead of earnings season.
Key events this week: US Core CPI Wed 10/14 (consensus +0.2% m/m), PPI and Retail Sales Thu 10/15, bank earnings Tue to Wed (JPM, WFC, Citi, BAC, MS), ASML Wed, TSM and ERIC Thu, AXP Fri.
